clue.text: Promise performance will provide verbal shenanigans

parts.note: to give your word is to promise
a play is a theatrical performance

explanation.surface: A promised show turns out to be all talk and trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning and other games with language are exactly the verbal tricks the clue describes.

clue.text: What's the point of setting?

parts.note: the compass point where the sun goes down each evening

explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' suggests a scene or a jewel's mount, and 'point' suggests purpose; it is the compass point of sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun sets towards that compass direction.

clue.text: Put up sound beams

indicators.note: the word for put up is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to raise is to put up

explanation.surface: Someone erects sturdy timber beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' gives RAISE, and 'sound' says the answer is spoken like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beams of light are rays.

clue.text: Quietly coming upon exotic arboreal creature

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Creeping silently upon some strange tree-dwelling animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming upon' only places the quiet letter first; 'arboreal' tempts you towards a tree-dweller like a koala, but its letters are the fodder for 'exotic'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic white bear is a large animal.

clue.text: Forgetting ecstatic feeling, having retired?

indicators.note: the word for retired holds the other two pieces inside it

parts.note: abed means having gone to bed, retired for the night
sent is old slang for thrilled or in ecstasy
mind in the sense of care or concern, as in 'do you mind?'

explanation.surface: An elated mood fades once the person has gone to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' works as a container: the bed-word has the two pieces inside it. 'Sent' as ecstatic is dated slang, as in 'the music sent me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forgetful, distracted person is said to be away with the fairies in this way.

clue.text: Don't fall behind changing parts for maintenance

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase trade places, the back part moving to the front

parts.note: to keep up is not to fall behind

explanation.surface: A coach urges a runner to stay with the pack while the team swaps spare parts for repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing parts' swaps KEEP and UP, giving UP before KEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of keeping something in good repair.

clue.text: Get overheated with normal companion

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Getting hot under the collar alongside an ordinary friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry out through heat, as the sun does to land or a throat.

clue.text: So. one entering means to stir the spirit?

indicators.note: the words for so and one go into the shuffled letters
stirring mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: thus means so
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking whether a single newcomer is the way to rouse a team's morale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' looks like a noun meaning method, but it is the anagram fodder for 'to stir'; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit in the sense of keen eagerness or zest.

clue.text: Nearly finished: plan to cover roof that's shot?

indicators.note: the word for plan is all but complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: a project is a plan
tiles are what cover a roof

explanation.surface: A builder close to completion worries about a roof that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly finished' cuts PROJECT to PROJEC; 'shot' looks like 'ruined' but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a missile fired from a gun.

clue.text: With cheats around, girl is given little scope

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for cheats is read backwards

parts.note: to gyp is to cheat, so gyps are cheats
lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl surrounded by swindlers is given little room to manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scope' here is short for telescope, not range or room to act; gyp, to swindle, is informal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope, a scope in miniature.

clue.text: Mostly unattractive, or primarily picturesque cave?

indicators.note: most of the word, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: grotty is British slang for unpleasant or unattractive

indicators.note: taking only the first letter of the word or

explanation.surface: Choose between an ugly cave and a pretty one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims GROTTY to GROTT; 'primarily' takes O from 'or'. GROTTY is everyday British slang for shabby or nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small, often ornamental cave of the kind found in landscaped gardens.

clue.text: Be fiddling with swapping starters engage best-known kitchen staff

indicators.note: the opening letters of the first and last pieces trade places

parts.note: to book is to engage, hire
the, stressed, means the best-known one
cooks staff a kitchen

explanation.surface: An instruction to hire a celebrity chef's team, by a fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOK THE COOKS with first letters swapped. 'Fiddling' means falsifying accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To falsify a firm's accounts is to fiddle them.

clue.text: MPs' shamelessness where tickets are available?

parts.note: front means brazen nerve or effrontery
belonging to MPs means of the House, the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A dig at the brazenness of politicians, set beside a question about the box office.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive MPs' is read as 'of (the) House', the Commons; the 'front' of a theatre is where the box office sits.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the public areas, foyer and box office included, are known as the front of the building.

clue.text: Obscure terms read in dash round shopping precinct

indicators.note: the word for dash goes round the shopping centre

parts.note: a sprint is a dash
a mall is a shopping precinct

explanation.surface: Fine print skimmed while racing round a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read in' is link padding; 'dash' is the noun for a short fast run, not punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions tucked into tiny type in a contract are easily missed.

clue.text: Flaunting manhood, but noble, not becoming blue —

definitions.text: Flaunting manhood, but noble, not becoming blue —

parts.words: Flaunting manhood, but noble, not becoming blue —
parts.note: nobles are said to have blue blood; a commoner whose blood stays its ordinary colour, and who flaunts his virility, fits

explanation.surface: A virile aristocrat refuses to turn blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue blood is the old mark of nobility, so blood that does not turn blue is the plain red kind, and that word also means virile.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lustily virile and vigorous is the sense of the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Nonsense from the detective I hired?

parts.note: a detective I hired is my detective
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: Dismissing the findings of a private investigator one has paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My eye!' is an old exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses scornful disbelief, like 'rubbish!'.

clue.text: New kit has me fuming at first this'll do for now

indicators.note: made new, so the letters are put into a fresh order
only the opening letter of the word fuming is used

explanation.surface: Someone furious about fresh kit settles for a temporary fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges KITHASME plus F, the first letter of 'fuming' picked by 'at first'.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift arrangement is a stopgap that serves until something better comes.

clue.text: — would it be so like a cheap novel?

definitions.text: — would it be so like a cheap novel?

parts.words: — would it be so like a cheap novel?
parts.note: carrying on from the clue before: a story that has not turned blue stays mild, and cheap novels are bound in paper

explanation.walkthrough: Continues the clue before it: not blue suggests mild or tame, and cheap novels are paperbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperback binding is the usual format of cheap fiction.

clue.text: Bully-boy grew up, lived and died here

definitions.text: Bully-boy grew up, lived and died here

parts.words: Bully-boy grew up, lived and died here
parts.note: the bull-boy is the Minotaur of Greek myth, half bull and half man, kept in the maze on Crete until Theseus killed him

explanation.surface: A thug's whole life spent in one place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully-boy' looks like a thug, but read it as bull-boy: the Minotaur, who lived out his life in Daedalus's maze.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan maze built by Daedalus housed the Minotaur from birth to death.

clue.text: Musket I left behind, having had endless bother

indicators.note: the letters for I and left come after the trimmed word
the final letter is cut from the word for bother

parts.note: fuss is bother or commotion

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a gun after it has caused nonstop trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' tells you the I and the L follow the trimmed bother-word rather than precede it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusil is a light flintlock musket.

clue.text: Failed to pass with second, and reinvested resources

parts.note: ploughed is old student slang for failed an exam
to back or second a proposal is to support it

explanation.surface: A student who flunked an exam is backed by a supporter and puts money back into the business.
explanation.walkthrough: To be ploughed was university slang for failing an exam; to second a motion is to back it.
explanation.definitionFit: Profits that are reinvested in a business rather than paid out are said to be returned to it.

clue.text: Allow for cash received

definitions.meaning: to ... a request is to allow it
a sum of money awarded, such as a student's award

explanation.definitionFit: Allowing a request and awarding a sum of money are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Disapproving of half of old furniture?

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for old furniture is used

parts.note: an antique is a piece of old furniture

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes half of a dusty old dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps ANTI from ANTIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is disapproving of it.

clue.text: Almost become good in spirit

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the word for become

parts.note: to grow is to become, as in grow old

explanation.surface: A soul that nearly turns good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts GROW to GRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum diluted with water was the sailors' drink.

clue.text: American originally going back to help in the pub?

indicators.note: the reversed help goes inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: An American original heads back to help out at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American originally' is the definition: the first Americans; 'pub' is inn, a British crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Native Americans, the continent's first inhabitants, were long called by this name.

clue.text: Bitter about straggling vine — remember seeing this?

indicators.note: the sour word is placed around the jumbled vine

parts.note: sour means bitter

indicators.note: a straggling vine sprawls untidily, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A sour gardener recalls an untidy vine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straggling' turns VINE into VENI, and SOUR goes 'about' it. The French verb behind the answer means 'to remember'.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is something kept to remind you of a place or event.

clue.text: The same thing seen around in gallery, until now

indicators.note: the reversed short form sits inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

indicators.note: the abbreviation is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same thing again

explanation.surface: Spotting a repeated exhibit in an art gallery, right up to the present.
explanation.walkthrough: Ditto marks are written 'do' in lists; the Tate is London's national gallery of art.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to the present moment.

clue.text: Unjustified assumption made for this process

definitions.text: Unjustified assumption made for this process

parts.words: Unjustified assumption made for this process
parts.note: assumption here is the taking on of power or a throne, not a guess; doing so without right is the process described

explanation.surface: A logician complains about a flawed premise in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumption' reads as a premise, but it means assuming office or power, done here without any right to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seizing a throne or position without lawful claim is exactly an unjustified taking of power.
